title: Passing to the schematic closure
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$ be any compactification
([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]) with $\overline X$ Noetherian, and let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be the schematic closure of $X$, with
$j_Z:X\hookrightarrow Z$ the induced open immersion
([sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure]). For a condensed coefficient ring
$\Lambda$, use its pulled-back coefficient sheaves on these schemes. For
every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_X)$ there are canonical
identifications, in $D(\overline X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_{\overline X})$
and $D(S_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_S)$ respectively,

$$
j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K,\qquad
Rp_*j_!K\simeq R(p\circ i)_*j_{Z,!}K.
$$

Thus, for schemes of finite type over $k$, replacing a compactification by
the schematic closure of $X$ does not change the expression $Rp_*j_!$
defining $Rf_!$; that expression needs only an open immersion followed by a
proper morphism.

proof.text: Use det-nagata-density-normalization-sheaves to obtain the sheaf isomorphism theta: j_! ≅ j_Z,! ⋙ i_*. Apply lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement to i and its quasi-compact complementary open in the Noetherian compactification, obtaining exactness of the actual condensed-module i_*. Pass theta termwise to the unbounded derived categories and compose with the inverse canonical exact-functor comparison Ri_* ≅ D(i_*). This supplies an isomorphism e: D(j_!) ≅ D(j_Z,!) ⋙ Ri_*.

The equality j_Z ; i = j and injectivity of the closed immersion i give i inverse-image of range(j) = range(j_Z). Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.isPullback makes the common-open square with vertical maps i and id_X a pullback. Apply lem-sfb-derived-open-restriction-normalization to that square. Its first conjunct makes the actual derived open-restriction mate invertible for arbitrary commutative condensed coefficients. The definition of identityOpenDerivedRestriction then composes that mate with the canonical derived identity comparison and right unitor, both isomorphisms, so the specified restriction r is invertible. No admissibility hypothesis or identity normalization formula is needed.

Normalize e by adjunction: transpose the unit of D(j_Z,!) ⊣ D(j_Z^*) followed by r inverse under D(j_!) ⊣ D(j^*). This is a natural transformation alpha: D(j_!) → D(j_Z,!) ⋙ Ri_*. The existing private openUnit proof in the sheaf-comparison module and Mathlib derived-adjunction-unit preservation make both open units invertible. The counit of D(j_!) is invertible on the target since e identifies that target with an object in its fully faithful image. Thus alpha is invertible. The Hom-bijection identity gives exactly unit_j ; D(j^*)(alpha) ; r = unit_j_Z, the first displayed normalization.

Whisker the normalized isomorphism by Rp_*, insert the functor associator, and whisker the inverse of the specified adjunction-normalized direct-image compositor. This is precisely the eS term in the statement; choose that composite, so its defining equality is reflexivity. This is the derived composition step of the unit proof. The geometry and quasi-compact open of det-nagata-density-normalization-setup make the closure another compactification. Only the public lowerComp definition is used, not the unrelated coordinateFace theorem in its defining module.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$ be any compactification
([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]) of separated schemes of finite type over a
field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be the schematic closure of $X$, with
$j_Z:X\hookrightarrow Z$ the induced open immersion
([sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure]). Let $\Lambda$ be the condensed coefficient
ring of a finite extension $E/\Ql$ or of $\Qlb$, and use its pulled-back
coefficient sheaves on these schemes. For every
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ there are canonical identifications, in
$D^b_c(\overline X,\Lambda)$ and $D^b_c(S,\Lambda)$ respectively,

$$
j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K,\qquad
Rp_*j_!K\simeq R(p\circ i)_*j_{Z,!}K.
$$

Thus replacing a compactification by the schematic closure of $X$ does not
change the expression $Rp_*j_!$ defining $Rf_!$; that expression needs only
an open immersion followed by a proper morphism.

proof.text:
The open and closed immersion operations on the pro-étale site are exact by
[sk-prop-sf-open-closed-triangle]. Its quasi-compact-open hypothesis applies
to the complement of $Z$ here because $\overline X$, being of finite type
over $k$, is Noetherian, and
therefore ensures exactness of $i_*$. Extension by zero along $j$ is
supported on $X$, which lies in $Z$. Its inverse image on $Z$ is extension by
zero along $j_Z$. Equivalently, the natural map

$$
j_!K\longrightarrow i_*i^*j_!K=i_*j_{Z,!}K
$$

is the identity on the open $X$ and both sides restrict to zero on its closed
complement. The open–closed localization sequence therefore makes it an
isomorphism. Since the immersion operations are exact, the argument applies
degreewise to complexes, in particular to bounded constructible ones.

Since $i_*$ is exact, $Ri_*=i_*$. The derived direct-image composition
isomorphism $Rp_*Ri_*\simeq R(p\circ i)_*$ proves the second
identification, as a composite of derived right adjoints.
